execute_graphql.notes: POST to the GraphQL endpoint, not /api/v4. Endpoint is derived from the REST base URL: take the origin plus everything before the trailing '/api/v4' in the base path, then append '/api/graphql' (e.g. https://git.example.com/gitlab/api/v4 -> https://git.example.com/gitlab/api/graphql). Overridable via GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL env var. Body: {"query": <query>, "variables": <variables or {}>}. Same auth headers as REST. Reference uses a 45s abort timeout. Read-only mode rejects mutation/subscription queries; modify mode rejects delete mutations. Returns the raw GraphQL JSON envelope (data/errors).

create_or_update_file.notes: Recorded method GET was the existence probe, not the write. Exact sequence in createOrUpdateFile(): (1) GET /projects/{project_id}/repository/files/{file_path}?ref={branch} via getFileContents (`branch` is required by the input schema, so the default-branch lookup inside getFileContents never runs). (2) If that GET succeeds the write method becomes PUT (update existing file) and, when the response is a single file object, body.commit_id / body.last_commit_id are filled from the caller's commit_id / last_commit_id when given, otherwise from the fetched file's commit_id / last_commit_id. If that GET fails with "File not found" (404) the write method stays POST (create) and only caller-supplied commit_id / last_commit_id are sent; any other error propagates. (3) The write goes to the SAME path /projects/{project_id}/repository/files/{file_path} with JSON body {branch, content, commit_message, encoding, previous_path?, commit_id?, last_commit_id?}. encoding = the `encoding` argument if given else GITLAB_REPO_FILE_ENCODING; content is passed through verbatim when `encoding` was supplied by the caller, otherwise re-encoded according to GITLAB_REPO_FILE_ENCODING. file_path is URL-encoded as a single path segment (slashes escaped), as is project_id.

create_branch.notes: Recorded record captured the resolver GET /projects/{project_id} (getDefaultBranchRef) instead of the real endpoint. Real call is createBranch(): POST /projects/{project_id}/repository/branches with JSON body {branch: <branch arg>, ref: <resolved ref>}. When the `ref` argument is omitted the case block first performs GET /projects/{project_id} and uses project.default_branch, falling back to the literal "main" when that field is null/absent; when `ref` is supplied no lookup happens. project_id is URL-encoded as a single path segment (slashes escaped).

mr_discussions.notes: Query params: page, per_page. project_id is URL-encoded as a single segment (slashes escaped). Reference wraps the response as {items: [...], pagination: {x_next_page, x_page, x_per_page, x_prev_page, x_total, x_total_pages}} read from the X-Next-Page/X-Page/X-Per-Page/X-Prev-Page/X-Total/X-Total-Pages response headers.

list_merge_request_note_emoji_reactions.notes: note_id is required; discussion_id is optional and only nests the note under /discussions/{discussion_id}/notes/.

delete_merge_request_emoji_reaction.notes: Empty response body; reference returns a fixed success string.

delete_merge_request_note_emoji_reaction.notes: Empty response body; reference returns a fixed success string.

create_issue_note.notes: JSON body: {"body": <body>} plus {"created_at": <created_at>} when created_at is supplied. discussion_id (when given) replies inside an existing thread.

delete_issue_emoji_reaction.notes: Empty response body; reference returns a fixed success string.

delete_issue_note_emoji_reaction.notes: Empty response body; reference returns a fixed success string.

list_issues.notes: listIssues() branches: `if (projectId || (ENABLE_STRICT_PROJECT_SCOPE && allowedProjectIds.length > 0))` it hits /projects/{effective project id}/issues, otherwise the instance-wide /issues. project_id is OPTIONAL in the input schema, so the instance-wide variant is reachable. Caveat for the branch condition: the project variant is also taken when project_id is omitted but GITLAB_PROJECT_ID / a strict-scope allowlist supplies a default (getEffectiveProjectId resolves it); with strict project scope enabled the instance-wide variant is never used. Every other argument is appended as a query param, except `labels` and `assignee_username`, which are appended as repeated `labels[]` / `assignee_username[]` entries (a non-array value is appended once under the [] key).

my_issues.notes: Two REST calls; the recorded `GET /user` was only the first (resolver) call. Sequence: (1) getCurrentUser() -> GET /user; if that responds 401/403 while a CI job token header is in use, it retries GET /job and takes `.user` from that body; any other failure aborts the tool. (2) listIssues(effectiveProjectId, opts) -> GET /projects/{project_id}/issues when a project id resolves, otherwise the instance-wide GET /issues (same branch as list_issues; project_id is optional and may be supplied by GITLAB_PROJECT_ID / strict-scope allowlist -- if getEffectiveProjectId throws the 'No project ID provided and GITLAB_PROJECT_ID is not set' error it is swallowed and the empty/instance-wide form is used). Filters sent on call 2: assignee_username[]=<current user's username>, or assignee_id=<current user's id> when the user has no username; state defaults to 'opened' when the arg is absent; labels, milestone, search, created_after, created_before, updated_after, updated_before, per_page, page are forwarded verbatim (labels goes out as repeated labels[] entries).

update_issue_description_patch.notes: Read-modify-write, up to three REST calls; the recorded `GET` was only the first (read) call. Sequence: (1) getIssue() -> GET /projects/{project_id}/issues/{issue_iid}, taking `description` (empty string when null). (2) Patch applied locally, no HTTP: patch_type='search_replace' parses `patch` into <<<<<<< SEARCH / ======= / >>>>>>> REPLACE blocks (throws 'No valid search/replace blocks found' when none parse; allow_multiple controls multi-occurrence replacement), patch_type='unified_diff' applies `patch` as a unified diff. (3) If dry_run is true the tool RETURNS HERE with a preview and makes no further calls. (4) updateIssue() -> PUT /projects/{project_id}/issues/{issue_iid} with body {"description": <patched text>} only. (5) If create_note is true, createIssueNote() -> POST /projects/{project_id}/issues/{issue_iid}/notes (top-level note, no discussion_id) with body {"body": "Updated issue description using patch-based tool.\n\n<summary>"}; a failure here is caught and reported in the result as note.status='failed' instead of failing the tool.

list_issue_discussions.notes: Query params: page, per_page. Same {items, pagination} envelope built from X-Next-Page/X-Page/X-Per-Page/X-Prev-Page/X-Total/X-Total-Pages headers as mr_discussions.

list_namespaces.notes: Query params: search, page, per_page, owned (booleans stringified). Reference builds this URL from the primary configured GITLAB_API_URL rather than the per-session effective API URL.

get_namespace.notes: namespace_id is encodeURIComponent-encoded (a full path like 'group/sub' becomes 'group%2Fsub'). Built from the primary configured GITLAB_API_URL.

verify_namespace.notes: The tool argument is literally named 'path'. It is encodeURIComponent-encoded into the URL. Optional query param: parent_id. Built from the primary configured GITLAB_API_URL.

list_projects.notes: Every supplied argument is forwarded verbatim as a query param (booleans as 'true'/'false'): search, search_namespaces, owned, membership, simple, archived, visibility, order_by, sort, with_issues_enabled, with_merge_requests_enabled, min_access_level, topic, page, per_page. Reference additionally filters the returned array through the project allowlist client-side.

list_project_members.notes: The selector is a truthiness check on include_inheritance: only include_inheritance=true selects /members/all; false or absent selects /members. Query params: query, per_page, page, plus repeated 'user_ids[]' and 'skip_users[]' entries for the user_ids / skip_users arrays.

list_group_members.notes: The selector is a truthiness check on include_inheritance: only include_inheritance=true selects /members/all; false or absent selects /members. Query params: query, per_page, page, plus repeated 'user_ids[]' and 'skip_users[]' entries for the user_ids / skip_users arrays.

get_label.notes: label_id may be a numeric id or a label name; it is encodeURIComponent-encoded. Optional query param include_ancestor_groups ('true'/'false'), sent only when explicitly provided.

update_label.notes: JSON body carries the remaining args: new_name, color, description, priority (project_id and label_id are stripped out of the body).

delete_label.notes: Empty response body; reference returns {status: 'success', message: 'Label deleted successfully'}.

get_repository_tree.notes: Query params: path, ref, recursive (only appended as 'true' when truthy), per_page, page_token, pagination. Keyset pagination token comes from the X-Next-Page-Token response header, falling back to X-Next-Page when pagination=keyset; the reference then returns {items, next_page_token, pagination_note} instead of a bare array whenever pagination=keyset or a token was returned. 404 is surfaced as 'Repository or path not found'.

get_pipeline_test_report.notes: Optional query params: page, per_page (only sent when defined). project_id is URL-encoded as a whole segment.

get_pipeline_test_report_summary.notes: Same helper as get_pipeline_test_report with summary=true (endpoint suffix test_report_summary). Optional query params: page, per_page.

create_deployment.notes: JSON body = all args except project_id: environment, sha, ref, tag, status.

update_deployment.notes: JSON body = { status }. 204 responses are reported as { success: true }.

delete_deployment.notes: No body. 204 responses are reported as { success: true }.

list_deployment_merge_requests.notes: Remaining args (page, per_page) become query params.

update_environment.notes: JSON body = remaining args: external_url, tier, auto_stop_setting.

delete_environment.notes: No body. 204 responses are reported as { success: true }.

stop_environment.notes: No body; `force` is sent as a QUERY param (only when defined), not in the body.

stop_stale_environments.notes: No body; `before` is sent as a QUERY param.

delete_review_app_environments.notes: No body; remaining args (before, limit, dry_run) are sent as QUERY params, stringified, only when defined.

list_pipeline_triggers.notes: Response must be redacted: strip `token`, `runners_token`, `import_url` from each item before returning to the model.

create_pipeline_trigger.notes: JSON body = { description }. Deliberately NOT redacted: the response carries the newly issued token once.

update_pipeline_trigger.notes: JSON body = { description }. Response must be redacted: strip `token`, `runners_token`, `import_url`.

delete_pipeline_trigger.notes: No body. 204 responses are reported as { success: true }.

list_ci_catalog_resources.notes: Sent through executeGitLabGraphQL (POST {origin}{prefix}/api/graphql, 45s abort timeout) which returns the RAW response body, so the tool result is the whole {"data":{...}} envelope, pretty-printed with JSON.stringify(result, null, 2). No result_path unwrapping and no client-side GraphQL-errors check. All eight variables are always present in the variables object; absent optional args are sent as JSON null/undefined (JSON.stringify drops undefined keys). first defaults to 20 when the arg is missing; zod already bounds it to 1..100. group_ids is an array of GroupID strings, topics an array of strings; scope/sort/verification_level are passed through as the uppercase enum strings the tool schema declares.
list_ci_catalog_resources.query:
query ListCiCatalogResources(
            $search: String,
            $first: Int,
            $after: String,
            $groupIds: [GroupID!],
            $scope: CiCatalogResourceScope,
            $sort: CiCatalogResourceSort,
            $topics: [String!],
            $verificationLevel: CiCatalogResourceVerificationLevel
          ) {
            ciCatalogResources(
              search: $search,
              first: $first,
              after: $after,
              groupIds: $groupIds,
              scope: $scope,
              sort: $sort,
              topics: $topics,
              verificationLevel: $verificationLevel
            ) {
              nodes {
                id
                name
                description
                fullPath
                icon
                starCount
                topics
                verificationLevel
                visibilityLevel
                webPath
                latestReleasedAt
                last30DayUsageCount
              }
              pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
            }
          }

get_ci_catalog_resource.notes: Exactly one of id / full_path must be supplied (zod union + refine: "Provide exactly one of id or full_path"); the other is sent as null. Sent through executeGitLabGraphQL, so the whole {"data":{...}} envelope is returned, pretty-printed with JSON.stringify(result, null, 2); no result_path unwrapping and no GraphQL-errors check. versionLimit/componentLimit/includeReadme are non-null GraphQL variables, hence the defaults 5 / 20 / false must always be filled in. Client-side post-filter: when component_name is set, for every node in data.ciCatalogResource.versions.nodes replace version.components.nodes with only the components whose name === component_name (versions whose components.nodes is not an array are left untouched); component_name is NOT sent to GraphQL. readme is only selected when includeReadme is true (@include directive).

play_pipeline_jobs.notes: For each id in job_ids, sequentially: (1) POST /projects/{project_id}/jobs/{job_id}/play with body { job_variables_attributes } (body only sent when job_variables_attributes is non-empty; the top-level job_inputs param is NOT passed by this tool); (2) poll GET /projects/{project_id}/jobs/{played.id} until job.status is terminal. Terminal job statuses: success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual. Poll interval = poll_interval_seconds (default 5s), overall deadline = timeout_seconds (default 300s) computed once per job at the start of that job's wait; each poll request carries an abort timeout equal to the remaining budget. If the deadline elapses before a terminal status: error 'Timed out waiting for terminal status'. Returns the array of completed job objects.

wait_for_pipeline.notes: Polls GET /projects/{project_id}/pipelines/{pipeline_id} until pipeline.status is terminal. Terminal pipeline statuses: success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual. Fetch once immediately, then sleep min(poll_interval_seconds*1000, remaining) between polls. poll_interval_seconds default 5, timeout_seconds default 300. 404 -> error 'Pipeline not found'. On timeout: error 'Timed out waiting for terminal status; last status: <status>'. Returns the final pipeline object.

wait_for_job.notes: Polls GET /projects/{project_id}/jobs/{job_id} until job.status is terminal. Terminal job statuses: success, failed, canceled, skipped, manual. Same waitForStatus loop as wait_for_pipeline: immediate first fetch, then sleep min(poll_interval_seconds*1000, remaining). poll_interval_seconds default 5, timeout_seconds default 300. 404 -> error 'Job not found'. On timeout: error 'Timed out waiting for terminal status; last status: <status>'. Returns the final job object.

list_merge_requests.notes: project_id is NOT required by the input schema. listMergeRequests branches: with a project_id (or under ENABLE_STRICT_PROJECT_SCOPE with a non-empty allowlist) it hits the project-scoped endpoint using getEffectiveProjectId(project_id); otherwise it hits the instance-wide GET /merge_requests, which returns the authenticated user's merge requests. Note the instance-wide branch does NOT fall back to GITLAB_PROJECT_ID — only the strict-scope allowlist forces the project branch. All remaining arguments become query params via appendMergeRequestFilters in both variants (labels joined with ',', approved_by_usernames emitted as approved_by_usernames[]=...).

get_users.notes: Not a single call to GET /users. The tool takes `usernames` (array of strings) and fans out: for each username, in array order and strictly sequentially (deliberately serial to avoid rate limiting), it issues GET /users?username=<username>. From the returned array it picks the entry whose `username` field matches the requested one exactly (case-sensitive, Array.prototype.find); if the array is empty or no exact match exists, the value is null. Any thrown error during a lookup (network failure or GitLab error from handleGitLabError) is caught and logged, and that username's value becomes null — a single failed lookup never fails the tool. The result is an object mapping every requested username -> user object or null (GitLabUsersResponseSchema).

get_commit_diff.notes: sha is encodeURIComponent-encoded. When full_diff is falsy the reference issues exactly one request with no pagination params and returns that array. When full_diff is true it loops page=1,2,3... appending ?page=N (per_page is left at the server default, which the reference assumes equals GITLAB_COMMIT_FILES_PER_PAGE) and concatenates results until a page returns fewer than that many entries.

health_check.notes: Takes no arguments. Sequence: (1) GET /user with the configured auth headers; authenticated = response.ok. (2) If not authenticated and the status is 401 or 403 and (GITLAB_JOB_TOKEN is set or usesJobTokenHeader()), GET /job; authenticated = jobResponse.ok. (3) If authenticated, GET /version (fetchGitLabVersionMetadata) and parse it into { version, revision, enterprise }; a non-ok response or any thrown error yields null and those fields are simply omitted — the version lookup never fails the health check. Neither the /user nor the /job response body is used, only response.ok. Returns { status: authenticated ? 'ok' : 'error', authenticated, gitlab_url: <effective API URL>, ...version metadata when available }. No handleGitLabError is called on any of the three requests.

download_release_asset.notes: direct_asset_path is a multi-segment path: encode each '/'-separated segment individually and keep the slashes (do NOT percent-encode the separators). tag_name is encoded as a single segment. Response is read as text, not JSON. In remote (IS_REMOTE) deployments the reference does not fetch at all and instead returns a proxied download_url plus the filename.

get_work_item.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. Sent through executeGraphQL (POST to <origin><prefix>/api/graphql, or GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL; throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array, then returns json.data). If data.namespace.workItem is null -> throw `Work item #<iid> not found in project <fullPath>`. The returned work item is flattened client-side: widgets[] are matched by __typename and folded into a lean object {id, iid, title, state, type, webUrl, + optional } — empty or null values are omitted.

list_work_items.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. ROOT FIELD SWITCH: the query root is `${rootField}` — literally `project` when the resolution above yielded kind=project and `group` when it yielded kind=group; `query` below shows the project form, and the group form is byte-identical with `project(fullPath: $path)` replaced by `group(fullPath: $path)`. result_path follows the same switch: ["data","group","workItems"] in the group case. transform `work_item_type_enums`: each element of types[] is mapped through {issue:ISSUE, task:TASK, incident:INCIDENT, test_case:TEST_CASE, epic:EPIC, key_result:KEY_RESULT, objective:OBJECTIVE, requirement:REQUIREMENT, ticket:TICKET}, falling back to the raw value with spaces -> underscores and uppercased. transform `state_passthrough`: state === "opened" ? "opened" : "closed" (lowercase, note the IssuableState enum is fed lowercase here). IMPORTANT: only `path` and `first` are always present in the variables object; types (only when the array is non-empty), state, search, assigneeUsernames (only when non-empty), labelName (only when non-empty) and after are added ONLY when supplied — absent filters are omitted rather than sent as null. The tool returns {items, pageInfo} where each item is a flattened {iid, title, state, type, webUrl} plus optional status/labels/assignees/weight/healthStatus/startDate/dueDate/milestone pulled out of widgets[].

list_work_item_statuses.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. transform `work_item_type_enum`: the lowercase tool enum is mapped through WORK_ITEM_TYPE_NAMES {issue:Issue, task:Task, incident:Incident, test_case:'Test Case', epic:Epic, key_result:'Key Result', objective:Objective, requirement:Requirement, ticket:Ticket} (unknown -> "Issue"), then spaces become underscores and the whole string is uppercased (e.g. test_case -> TEST_CASE). (work_item_type defaults to "issue" -> "ISSUE"). Sent through executeGraphQL (POST to <origin><prefix>/api/graphql, or GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL; throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array, then returns json.data). A missing or empty data.namespace.workItemTypes.nodes throws `Work item type '<DisplayName>' not found in project`. Only nodes[0] is used; the tool returns the remapped {work_item_type: node.name, statuses_available: statuses.length > 0, statuses} where statuses come from the widgetDefinitions entry whose __typename is "WorkItemWidgetDefinitionStatus" (allowedStatuses, else []), plus optional supported_conversion_types (node.supportedConversionTypes names), allowed_child_types and allowed_parent_types (names from the "WorkItemWidgetDefinitionHierarchy" entry) — each added only when non-empty. Requires Premium/Ultimate with configurable statuses.

list_custom_field_definitions.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. transform `work_item_type_enum`: the lowercase tool enum is mapped through WORK_ITEM_TYPE_NAMES {issue:Issue, task:Task, incident:Incident, test_case:'Test Case', epic:Epic, key_result:'Key Result', objective:Objective, requirement:Requirement, ticket:Ticket} (unknown -> "Issue"), then spaces become underscores and the whole string is uppercased (e.g. test_case -> TEST_CASE). (work_item_type defaults to "issue" -> "ISSUE"). Sent through executeGraphQL (POST to <origin><prefix>/api/graphql, or GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL; throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array, then returns json.data). A missing or empty data.namespace.workItemTypes.nodes throws `Work item type '<DisplayName>' not found in project`. Only nodes[0] is used; the tool returns {work_item_type: node.name, custom_fields: [...]}, each entry remapped from the "WorkItemWidgetDefinitionCustomFields" widget's customFieldValues[].customField as {id, name, type: fieldType, selectOptions? (only when non-empty), workItemTypes? (names, only when non-empty)}.

move_work_item.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. TWO such resolutions happen, in order: project_id -> $projectPath and target_project_id -> $targetProjectPath, i.e. two REST calls (GET /projects/{project_id} then GET /projects/{target_project_id}); the pre_step below describes the first, target_project_id goes through the identical procedure. $iid is String(iid). Sent through executeGraphQL (POST to <origin><prefix>/api/graphql, or GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL; throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array, then returns json.data). If data.issueMove.errors is non-empty -> throw `Failed to move work item: <errors joined by ", ">`. Returns data.issueMove.issue as-is ({id, iid, webUrl}).

list_work_item_notes.notes: transform `resolved_full_path` = resolveProjectOrGroupPath(project_id): decodeURIComponent(project_id), then match ^(group|project):(.+)$ — an explicit `group:` prefix is refused outright while GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (or a session scope) is non-empty; the remainder is passed through getEffectiveProjectId (GITLAB_PROJECT_ID override). With an explicit `group:` prefix it does GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and takes `full_path` (kind=group). Otherwise GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and takes `path_with_namespace` (kind=project); only if that 404s AND there was no explicit prefix AND the allowlist is empty AND the id is not all digits does it retry GET /groups/{urlencoded id} and use `full_path` (kind=group). This REST call always happens — it is NOT skipped for path-like ids. All five variables are ALWAYS sent: pageSize = page_size || 20, after = after || null (explicit null, not omitted), sort = sort || "CREATED_ASC". Sent through executeGraphQL (POST to <origin><prefix>/api/graphql, or GITLAB_GRAPHQL_URL; throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array, then returns json.data). A null data.namespace.workItem throws `Work item #<iid> not found in project <fullPath>`. result_path stops at the workItem because the discussions connection is then located by scanning workItem.widgets[] for the first entry that HAS a `discussions` key (the WorkItemWidgetNotes fragment). The tool returns {discussions, pageInfo: discussions.pageInfo || {}} where each discussion is remapped to {id, notes: [{id, author: author.username, body, createdAt, system? , internal?, lastEditedAt?}], resolved? , resolvable?} — the optional keys are added only when truthy.

list_work_item_note_emoji_reactions.notes: Sent through executeGraphQL, which throws on a non-2xx response and on a non-empty top-level `errors` array before returning `json.data`. Missing/null awardable or awardEmoji yields an empty array `[]` rather than an error. NOTE: project_id and iid are declared required in the tool schema but the reference implementation ignores them for this tool — only note_id (and name) reach GraphQL; note_id must already be a note GID such as gid://gitlab/Note/123, it is passed through verbatim with no conversion.

create_work_item_note_emoji_reaction.notes: Sent through executeGraphQL (throws on HTTP error and on a non-empty top-level `errors`). Additionally: if data.awardEmojiAdd.errors is non-empty, throw `Failed to add emoji reaction: <errors joined by ", ">`. Otherwise return data.awardEmojiAdd.awardEmoji as-is. NOTE: project_id and iid are declared required in the tool schema but the reference implementation ignores them for this tool — only note_id (and name) reach GraphQL; note_id must already be a note GID such as gid://gitlab/Note/123, it is passed through verbatim with no conversion.

delete_work_item_note_emoji_reaction.notes: Sent through executeGraphQL (throws on HTTP error and on a non-empty top-level `errors`). Additionally: if data.awardEmojiRemove.errors is non-empty, throw `Failed to remove emoji reaction: <errors joined by ", ">`. If the unwrapped awardEmoji is null/undefined the tool returns the literal object {"status":"success","message":"Work item note emoji reaction removed"} instead. NOTE: project_id and iid are declared required in the tool schema but the reference implementation ignores them for this tool — only note_id (and name) reach GraphQL; note_id must already be a note GID such as gid://gitlab/Note/123, it is passed through verbatim with no conversion.

list_webhooks.notes: project_id wins when both are supplied; group_id is required when project_id is absent. Query params: page, per_page.

create_webhook.notes: project_id wins when both are supplied. JSON body is every defined argument except project_id, group_id and hook_id (i.e. url, name, description, token, signing_token, enable_ssl_verification, all *_events flags, push_events_branch_filter, branch_filter_strategy, custom_webhook_template, custom_headers).

update_webhook.notes: project_id wins when both are supplied. JSON body is every defined argument except project_id, group_id and hook_id. hook_id is interpolated raw (numeric).

delete_webhook.notes: project_id wins when both are supplied. Empty response body; reference returns {status: 'deleted', hook_id}.

list_webhook_events.notes: project_id wins when both are supplied. Query params always set: page (default 1), per_page (default 20; GitLab caps webhook events at 20). status is appended when provided. The 'summary' argument is client-side only: when true the reference condenses each event instead of returning the raw objects.

get_webhook_event.notes: No single endpoint for one event: the reference pages GET /projects/{project_id}/hooks/{hook_id}/events (or GET /groups/{group_id}/hooks/{hook_id}/events when project_id is absent) with per_page=20 and finds the entry whose id === event_id. If the 'page' argument is supplied it fetches only that one page and returns the match or null. Otherwise it walks pages 1..25 (up to 500 events), stopping early when a page returns fewer than 20 events or a match is found. Not found -> reference returns an error object stating the event was not found 'on page N' / 'in the 500 most recent events'.

search_code.notes: Instance-wide blob search. Query params: scope=blobs (always), search, plus optional page, per_page, filename, path, extension. Note the 'path' argument is a query param here, not a path segment.

search_project_code.notes: Query params: scope=blobs (always), search, plus optional ref, page, per_page, filename, path, extension. The 'path' argument is a query param, not a path segment.

search_group_code.notes: Query params: scope=blobs (always), search, plus optional page, per_page, filename, path, extension. The 'path' argument is a query param, not a path segment. group_id is encoded segment-wise (slashes preserved) in the reference, unlike project_id.

list_group_variables.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. group_id is decoded then URL-encoded as one segment. Query params: page, per_page; the object-valued `filter` arg is flattened to filter[<key>]=<value> (e.g. filter[environment_scope]=production).

get_group_variable.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. filter.environment_scope is sent as query param filter[environment_scope].

create_group_variable.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. JSON body = all args except group_id: key, value, variable_type, protected, masked, raw, environment_scope, description.

update_group_variable.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. JSON body = args except group_id, key and filter (value, variable_type, protected, masked, raw, environment_scope, description). filter.environment_scope goes into the query string as filter[environment_scope].

delete_group_variable.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. filter.environment_scope is sent as query param filter[environment_scope]. Response body ignored; tool returns a synthetic success message.

get_dependency_proxy_settings.notes: group_id is resolved to a group full path first: decodeURIComponent(group_id); if the decoded value is all digits, GET /groups/{decoded} and take `full_path`; otherwise the decoded value is used as-is (transform `resolved_full_path`). Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment — the tool is refused outright when the server runs in project-scoped deployment mode. Sent through executeGraphQL (throws on HTTP error and on a non-empty top-level `errors`). If data.group is null -> throw `Group not found: <fullPath>`. The unwrapped group object is then remapped before being returned: {enabled: group.dependencyProxySetting?.enabled ?? false, blob_count: group.dependencyProxyBlobCount, total_size: group.dependencyProxyTotalSize, image_prefix: group.dependencyProxyImagePrefix, ttl_policy: group.dependencyProxyImageTtlPolicy} (ttl_policy keeps its GraphQL shape {enabled, ttl}).

update_dependency_proxy_settings.notes: Pre-validation: if none of enabled / identity / secret is supplied -> throw `At least one of enabled, identity, or secret must be provided` without contacting GitLab. group_id is resolved to a group full path first: decodeURIComponent(group_id); if the decoded value is all digits, GET /groups/{decoded} and take `full_path`; otherwise the decoded value is used as-is (transform `resolved_full_path`). Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment — the tool is refused outright when the server runs in project-scoped deployment mode. transform `dependency_proxy_settings_input` builds the single GraphQL variable `input` as an object: {groupPath: <resolved_full_path>} plus, only for the args that were actually supplied (undefined keys are omitted, not sent as null), enabled <- enabled (boolean), identity <- identity (string), secret <- secret (string). Sent through executeGraphQL. If data.updateDependencyProxySettings.errors is non-empty -> throw `Failed to update dependency proxy settings: <errors joined by ", ">`. The mutation's own payload is discarded: on success the executor must re-run the get_dependency_proxy_settings query with the SAME already-resolved fullPath (no second REST resolution) and return that remapped settings object — i.e. {enabled, blob_count, total_size, image_prefix, ttl_policy}.

list_dependency_proxy_blobs.notes: group_id is resolved to a group full path first: decodeURIComponent(group_id); if the decoded value is all digits, GET /groups/{decoded} and take `full_path`; otherwise the decoded value is used as-is (transform `resolved_full_path`). Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment — the tool is refused outright when the server runs in project-scoped deployment mode. Sent through executeGraphQL. If data.group?.dependencyProxyBlobs is missing -> throw `Group not found or dependency proxy not enabled: <fullPath>`. The unwrapped connection is remapped before returning: {blobs: nodes.map(n => ({file_name: n.fileName, size: n.size, created_at: n.createdAt})), pageInfo: connection.pageInfo}.

purge_dependency_proxy_cache.notes: Guarded by rejectIfProjectScopedDeployment. group_id decoded then URL-encoded as one segment; no query or body. Response body ignored; tool returns a synthetic 'purge scheduled' message.

list_project_vulnerabilities.notes: The REST vulnerabilities API is deprecated (it silently ignores filters), so this is GraphQL-only. transform `resolved_full_path`: project_id is decoded, run through getEffectiveProjectId (the GITLAB_PROJECT_ID env override can replace it) and decoded again; if the result is all digits, GET /projects/{urlencoded id} and take `path_with_namespace` (throw `Could not resolve full path for project <id>` when absent); otherwise the decoded path is used as-is. transform `min_100`: Math.min(first ?? 20, 100). transform `upper_single_array`: the lowercase enum arg becomes a one-element array of its uppercased form, e.g. state "secret_detection" -> ["SECRET_DETECTION"]. IMPORTANT: state, severity, reportType and after are only added to the variables object when the corresponding arg is present — absent filters are omitted entirely rather than sent as null (fullPath and first are always sent). Sent through executeGraphQL (throws on HTTP error and on a non-empty top-level `errors`). If data.project is null -> throw `Project not found or not accessible: <fullPath>`. The tool returns {vulnerabilities: <unwrapped>.nodes, pageInfo: <unwrapped>.pageInfo}.

get_vulnerability.notes: transform `vulnerability_gid` (toVulnerabilityGid): an all-digits id becomes `gid://gitlab/Vulnerability/<n>`; a value already matching ^gid://gitlab/Vulnerability/\d+$ is passed through unchanged; anything else -> throw `Invalid vulnerability ID "<id>": expected a numeric ID or a gid://gitlab/Vulnerability/<id> global ID`. Sent through executeGraphQL (throws on HTTP error and on a non-empty top-level `errors`). If data.vulnerability is null -> throw `Vulnerability not found: <vulnerability_id>`. Post-check: because vulnerability GIDs are global rather than project-scoped, the returned `project` block is validated against GITLAB_ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS (no-op when that allowlist is empty) — allowed if the allowlist contains project.fullPath or the numeric id parsed out of project.id (^gid://gitlab/Project/(\d+)$), otherwise throw `Access denied: Vulnerability <id> belongs to project <fullPath|numericId|unknown>, which is not in the allowed project list: <ids joined by ", ">`. The whole vulnerability object (including the extra project { id name fullPath } selection) is returned.

discover_tools.notes: Meta-tool handled before the GitLab dispatch switch; makes no HTTP call. With no 'category' argument it returns the list of toolset definitions as {categories: [{id, toolCount, active, isDefault}], hint}. With a category it validates the name against the known toolset ids (error result listing valid ids if unknown) and otherwise activates that toolset, mutating the exposed tool list and emitting a tools/list_changed notification.
